facts.raw_span: 87-year-old Cantonese-speaking man
Alzheimer’s dementia, hypertension, stroke, hyperlipidaemia, gout, peptic ulcer, and chronic kidney disease
one week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
impaired mobility
a single episode of urinary incontinence
anorexia and a 12% body-weight loss over six months
blood pressure was 88/45 mmHg
heart rate 96/min
elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.5 × 10^9/L)
pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury
bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy
no evidence of trochanteric bursitis

concepts.why: Elevated inflammatory markers and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement are consistent with an iliopsoas abscess.
Elevated inflammatory markers and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement are consistent with pyomyositis.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with elevated inflammatory markers, are consistent with septic arthritis of the hip.
History of gout and increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with anorexia and weight loss, are consistent with crystal arthropathy.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with elevated inflammatory markers, are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with anorexia and weight loss, are consistent with polymyalgia rheumatica.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with elevated inflammatory markers, are consistent with osteomyelitis.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement, are consistent with spondyloarthritis.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with left-sided insertional tendinopathy, are consistent with iliopsoas tendinitis.
History of gout and increasing left leg pain and weakness are consistent with chronic tophaceous gout.
It explains the low blood pressure finding of 88/45 mmHg.
It explains the pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury.

rationales.F01: Age is not specific to any condition
rationales.F02: Multiple comorbidities increase the likelihood of various conditions
rationales.F03: Left leg pain and weakness could be indicative of several conditions
rationales.F05: Urinary incontinence could be related to neurological or urinary conditions
rationales.F06: Weight loss and anorexia could be indicative of chronic disease or malignancy
rationales.F07: Hypotension could be related to dehydration or sepsis
rationales.F09: Elevated inflammatory markers suggest an infectious or inflammatory condition
rationales.F10: Pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury suggests kidney disease exacerbation
rationales.F11: Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement is highly suggestive of iliopsoas abscess or pyomyositis
rationales.F12: No evidence of trochanteric bursitis rules out this condition

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated inflammatory markers and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement support Pyomyositis, which is a more specific diagnosis than Iliopsoas abscess given the patient's presentation and imaging findings.
